title: A Bio-Refinery Concept for N and P Recovery—A Chance for Biogas Plant Development
geography: Experimental Dairy Farm De Marke, Hengelo (Gld), Netherlands
material_scope: Cattle slurry anaerobic digestion; digestate solid-liquid separation; liquid digestate struvite precipitation and ammonia stripping to ammonium sulfate
license: CC BY 4.0 (stated in full-text article footer)
exact_locations: Methods 2.2; Table 1; Table 2; Results and Discussion; Conclusions
data_handling: Transcribed reported means and SDs where present, preserving wet-basis denominators, source terminology and study-specific recovery definitions. No values inferred from plots, missing flowrates, or stoichiometry.
limitations: The process digested cattle slurry, not roadside grass or GreenHub protein-extraction residues; matrix-specific values must not become GreenHub defaults.
Analyses were performed in triplicate, but process flowrates and a closed mass/element balance across the recovery train are not reported in the extracted records.

Source-reported N and P recovery percentages are differences between feed and final-effluent concentrations; they are not independently validated mass recoveries, and the reported N value combines struvite precipitation and ammonia stripping.
Struvite is a medium-purity mixed product with organic and mineral impurities. Ammonium sulfate is a dilute, acidic solution, not a dry fertilizer product grade.

The source reports cattle-slurry farm-scale conditions; these observations support comparator and product-specification research only, not GreenHub recovery equations, reagent demand, price-grade matching, or LCA factors.
